title: rarn.lock
description: Rarn lockfile. Records the exact, fully resolved dependency graph so that any machine reproduces byte-identical install output. Generated — never hand-edited. Written with sorted keys and a trailing newline so diffs stay reviewable.

lockfileVersion.description: Bumped only on a breaking format change. A newer lockfileVersion than the CLI understands is a hard error, not a warning. It tracks the format and not the release: reaching 1.0.0 does not move it, because bumping for ceremony would invalidate every lockfile already on disk for nothing and would teach the next reader that the number follows version numbers. If a breaking change is ever needed it lands as 2, in whatever release carries it.

registry.description: API base URL every 'resolved' field in this file points at.

root.description: Snapshot of everything in rarn.json that could change the resolution. Comparing it against the current manifest is how 'rarn install' decides whether the lockfile can be reused without contacting the registry at all. It deliberately excludes fields that only affect linking — packageDir, place, aliases — because linking runs on every install regardless.

registry.description: The manifest's "registry" — the *index repository*, not the API. Distinct from the top-level `registry` field, which records the API base the `resolved` URLs point at. Pointing the manifest at a different index can change which versions exist, so it belongs in the snapshot.

resolutions.description: Overrides in force when this lockfile was written. Recorded because changing one changes the resolution, and a lockfile that did not notice would keep installing the version the user just overrode.

packages.description: Every resolved package, keyed by '@scope/name@version'. One entry per (name, version) pair — two entries sharing a name means dedupe could not collapse them, which 'rarn dedupe' reports.

version.description: Exact resolved version. Never a range.

resolved.description: Absolute package-contents URL the archive was fetched from.

integrity.description: Hash of the downloaded ZIP bytes, verified on every install. A mismatch aborts.

realm.description: Realm the registry declares for this version. A 'shared' package may only depend on other 'shared' packages; a 'server' package may depend on anything.

placement.description: Which install directory this package actually lands in — the resolved origin realm, which is NOT always the declared realm. When several requesters disagree, the widest placement wins (shared > server > dev), because a package must live where its most permissive requester can still see it. A shared package pulled in only by a dev dependency is placed in 'dev'.

moduleRoot.description: Path inside the extracted archive that held the module tree, as resolved from the package's default.project.json. Absent means the whole archive was copied. Informational only: installing re-derives this from the cached archive rather than trusting the record, since re-reading one small file is cheaper than the class of bug where a stale lockfile silently changes what gets installed.

indexDir.description: Folder name under _Index, in Wally's own '{scope}_{name}@{version}' form.

dependencies.description: This package's own dependencies, mapping the alias its source code requires to the packageKey that alias resolves to. The linker turns each entry into one sibling shim inside the package's _Index folder.

requestedBy.description: Every requester and the range it asked for. Powers 'rarn why' and makes dedupe conflicts explainable rather than mysterious.

from.description: A packageKey, or the literal 'root' for a direct dependency of rarn.json.

range.description: The range as requested, already normalized to npm syntax.

dev.description: True when this package is reachable only through devDependencies. Skipped by 'rarn install --production'.

integrity.description: Subresource-Integrity style: 'sha256-' followed by the base64 digest.

alias.description: Shim filename, minus the extension. Comes from the package's own metadata rather than from anything Rarn chose, so it has to accept what the registry actually contains - jsdotlua/luau-polyfill declares dependencies called es7-types, instance-of and symbol-luau. A stricter pattern here made install write a lockfile it then refused to read.
